dimension_justifications.soundness: The conditional finite-pool definition and displayed decomposition arithmetic are internally correct, and the paper appropriately avoids causal, calibration, and decoder-expectation conclusions. However, the empirical inputs, treatment, score construction, sample, and decoder traces are all unavailable, so the central source-reported quantities cannot be verified or scientifically interpreted beyond transcription.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The four-page paper is clear, candid about its boundary, well localized, anonymous, and within the ICLR main-text limit. Tables and equations make the limited arithmetic audit easy to follow. Some terminology, especially the source-described intervention and commit score, necessarily remains opaque because its definitions are absent.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The verified contribution is a careful restatement of a conditional descriptive estimand and an inventory of missing artifacts. This is useful quality-control documentation, but without auditable source records or a new empirical/methodological result it is too narrow to establish a substantial ICLR contribution.

paper_summary: This paper audits two source-reported GSM8K/LLaDA records: a natural-strata cross-level score-minus-correctness contrast of +0.2227 and a separate 400-item, source-described paired fixed-filler contrast of -0.0075. It formalizes the latter as a finite-pool, one-recorded-decode descriptive contrast, verifies only printed arithmetic, and explicitly states that missing records prevent causal, calibration, decoder-average, or cross-record conclusions.
strongest_verified_contribution: The paper correctly separates the two records' samples and estimands, defines a finite-pool contrast conditional on stored single-decode outputs (PDF p. 2, Sec. 3), and correctly checks the natural-strata printed identity -0.0314 - (-0.2541) = +0.2227 (PDF p. 3, Sec. 4.1).
strengths: The paper makes unusually explicit that the two reported point values have different samples and estimands and should not be jointly compared (PDF pp. 1, 3).
The formal definition in Sec. 3 correctly limits the paired quantity to the named pool and recorded realization rather than silently treating it as a population or decoder expectation.
The manuscript transparently labels empirical values as source-reported/cannot-verify and does not misrepresent unavailable artifacts as rerun evidence.

The arithmetic in Table 2 and the reported Table 3 contrast are consistent with the printed precision; the manuscript appropriately identifies the arm-mean subtraction discrepancy as rounding opacity rather than a demonstrated numerical error.
questions: Can the authors provide an immutable item manifest, literal filler and insertion rule, serialized prompts, tokenizer-dose check, paired rows, decoding traces/configuration, score-to-answer aggregation definition, and analysis reproducer for A32-E2?
What exactly is the scalar commit score s_i: which token positions are aggregated, how is the aggregation performed, and what event—if any—does it forecast?
Can the source record for A32-E1 provide group membership, exclusions, overlap with A32-E2, and the analysis that generated the high-minus-low components?

issues.location: PDF p. 2, Secs. 2-3; PDF p. 3, Sec. 4.2 and Table 3; reviewer-safe evidence/repository_inventory.md and experiment_registry.json (A32-X2).
issues.observed_evidence: The package contains neither the 400-item manifest/selection rule, literal filler, insertion location, tokenizer verification, paired rows, prompts, decode traces, execution configuration, nor analysis code. Table 3 is explicitly source-reported only.
issues.why_it_matters: Consequently, neither the claimed paired treatment contrast nor its numerical value can be independently reconstructed. The formal contrast is valid only as a definition conditional on an unspecified stored record; it cannot establish that a +37-token fixed-filler intervention was actually implemented or that the reported arms are paired as stated.
issues.required_fix: Release a reviewer-auditable, immutable protocol and artifacts for A32-E2, or further recast the paper as documentation of an unverified transcription rather than evidence about a paired filler record.
issues.verification_test: Recompute every Table 3 arm mean and Long-minus-Short contrast from per-item paired rows using the released manifest, prompts, exact filler/tokenizer fixture, score procedure, correctness matcher, and frozen decode configuration.
issues.evidence_needed: The complete A32-E2 manifest, protocol, prompts, treatment fixture, traces, item-level scores/outcomes, model/tokenizer revisions, and deterministic analysis script.

issues.location: PDF p. 1, Abstract and Sec. 1, lines 35-41; PDF p. 2, Sec. 3, lines 88-104; PDF p. 4, Sec. 6, lines 170-174; reviewer-safe evidence/method_provenance.tsv, A32-M1.
issues.observed_evidence: The manuscript states that token-to-answer aggregation and forecast-event semantics are unavailable and that the score is not verified as a probability of final-answer correctness. It nevertheless centers the statistic s_i minus y_i as a score-outcome quantity.
issues.why_it_matters: The algebra is defined for any scalar s_i, but without the score construction and its relation to the final answer, the scientific interpretation of its level, sign, and movement is unresolved. The paper correctly avoids calling it calibration, but this limitation also means the reported statistic is not yet evidence of a meaningful decoder uncertainty or answer-quality phenomenon.
issues.required_fix: Specify and validate the score construction and target event, or retain only a clearly non-semantic source-record transcription and correspondingly narrow the claimed contribution.
issues.verification_test: From released traces and code, reproduce s_i for sampled items; document token positions and aggregation; then test whether the stated score corresponds to the claimed final-answer event under the source matcher.
issues.evidence_needed: Score/readout implementation, token traces, answer aggregation rule, correctness matcher, and construct-validation analysis.

issues.location: PDF p. 1, Abstract and Sec. 1 contribution list; PDF p. 3, Sec. 4.1 and Table 2; reviewer-safe evidence/experiment_registry.json, A32-X1; reviewer-safe evidence/claim_evidence_map.tsv, A32-C1.
issues.observed_evidence: A32-E1 is marked source_reported_not_rerun and lacks item records, strata construction, overlap map, and analysis code. The paper can check only the displayed identity, not the natural-strata measurement or even its sample construction.
issues.why_it_matters: The +0.2227 contextual record is a central motivating datum, but the package cannot establish its provenance or empirical content. Transparency about this fact is a strength, yet it leaves no independently supported empirical result on which to ground the paper's broader relevance.
issues.required_fix: Provide the A32-E1 data/analysis and its relationship to A32-E2, or remove the number from the central empirical framing and present it solely as an unverifiable quoted record.
issues.verification_test: Reconstruct high/low strata from the released item identities and length rule, reproduce the component means and +0.2227, and produce an overlap/exclusion report relative to A32-E2.
issues.evidence_needed: A32-E1 item-level records, stratum rule, length computation, exclusions, score/outcome values, analysis code, and overlap map.

issues.location: PDF p. 1, Sec. 1, lines 32-34; PDF p. 4, References; reviewer-safe citation_lock.json/citation_lock.json.
issues.observed_evidence: The included citation lock verifies the signed-summary and neighboring-prompt-calibration boundaries, but does not provide reviewer-safe verification for the GSM8K and LLaDA citations used to identify the source setting.
issues.why_it_matters: This does not undermine the paper's explicitly source-reported framing, but it prevents independent checking of the contextual model/task attribution from the supplied package.
issues.required_fix: Include verified citation metadata/support records for the contextual model and benchmark citations, or mark these setting labels as unverified source attributions.
issues.verification_test: Match the cited primary sources to the stated benchmark and model descriptions and verify that the local wording does not exceed their support.
issues.evidence_needed: Citation-lock entries or primary-source excerpts/metadata for Cobbe et al. (2021) and Nie et al. (2025).

ethics_concerns: No direct human-subject, privacy, or deployment harm is claimed. The main responsible-research concern is epistemic: readers could overread source-reported values as verified experiments, which the manuscript substantially mitigates through repeated limitations statements.
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by an isolated AI subagent for internal pre-submission quality control, using only the frozen submission snapshot.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A fully auditable release for A32-E1 and A32-E2 that reproduces the printed records and establishes sample, treatment, score, and decoder provenance.
A precise score definition plus evidence relating it to a specified final-answer event, with the paper's claims updated to match that validation.
Paired replay or multi-seed evidence if the authors seek any conclusion beyond the stored-realization finite-pool contrast.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Reproduction showing that Table 2 or Table 3 values do not follow from the underlying records.
Artifacts showing that the Long arm was not a paired fixed-filler-only modification, that the stated token dose/configuration is wrong, or that score/outcome matching differs across arms.
Evidence that the source score cannot be reduced to a consistently defined scalar per item as assumed by the formal display.
review_limitations: The frozen package intentionally excludes the underlying experimental artifacts, so empirical claims can only be classified as cannot_verify rather than falsified.
I assessed the supplied PDF and reviewer-safe evidence/citation material only; I did not inspect any external source, repository history, or prior review material.
